key_insight: CausalForge combines Lean-verified formal proofs with a self-improving agent pipeline to automate theoretical research in causal inference while checking that formal theorems still match the intended informal claims.
engineering_relevance: The framework offers a practical template for trustworthy AI-assisted theorem proving and research automation by pairing kernel verification with human-auditable statement audits.
method: Causalean: a Lean causal inference library with 7,035 machine-checked declarations.
CausalSmith: an agentic loop that picks topics, proposes results, formalizes statements, proves them, and packages artifacts.
Statement audit: compares each formal theorem to its intended scientific claim beyond proof checking.
evidence_signal: The system is evaluated on artifacts generated by completed autonomous research runs, with source code, the formal library, and run records released publicly on GitHub.
watch_item: Machine-checked proofs do not guarantee the formal statement faithfully captures the intended research claim, so statement auditing remains a critical failure point.
paper_title: CausalForge: A Formally Grounded, Self-Improving Agentic Framework for Automated Research in Causal Inference
